Order data, aggregate intervals, and exploit monotonic structure.

This family contains **11 independently navigable LeetCode topics**. Each topic has its own directory and a starting mathematical abstraction. The grouping is a learning aid, not part of LeetCode's official hierarchy.

## Topics

1. **[Sorting](../sorting/index.qmd)** — Reorder a collection according to a comparison rule.
2. **[Merge Sort](../merge-sort/index.qmd)** — Recursively sort halves and merge their ordered outputs.
3. **[Counting Sort](../counting-sort/index.qmd)** — Count discrete keys in a bounded domain to construct sorted output.
4. **[Bucket Sort](../bucket-sort/index.qmd)** — Distribute keys into buckets, sort locally, and concatenate.
5. **[Radix Sort](../radix-sort/index.qmd)** — Sort positional digits with a stable subroutine.
6. **[Monotonic Stack](../monotonic-stack/index.qmd)** — Maintain candidate indices whose values follow a monotonic invariant.
7. **[Monotonic Queue](../monotonic-queue/index.qmd)** — Maintain an ordered deque of undominated candidates in a sliding window.
8. **[Prefix Sum](../prefix-sum/index.qmd)** — Precompute cumulative aggregates for efficient interval queries.
9. **[Segment Tree](../segment-tree/index.qmd)** — Store associative aggregates over a recursively partitioned range.
10. **[Binary Indexed Tree](../binary-indexed-tree/index.qmd)** — Represent prefix aggregates through binary-indexed intervals.
11. **[Sweep Line](../sweep-line/index.qmd)** — Process geometric or time events in sorted order while maintaining active state.

## Mathematical connection

A problem can carry several topic labels. Let $P$ be a problem and $\mathcal T$ the set of all tags. Its topic assignment is a set-valued mapping:

$$
L:P\longrightarrow\mathcal P(\mathcal T).
$$

Here $L(p)$ is the set of tags assigned to problem $p$. Tags describe relevant structures and techniques; they do **not** uniquely determine an algorithm or a proof of correctness.
